persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Mike, 40, a father in Illinois, USA. His daughter Emma, 12, plays basketball for a team called Gold Rush in her church's league. Many churches in America run sports leagues for children on Saturdays. Today is Friday night, and you need to know where and when Emma plays, and what to bring.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called GameDay. You have never seen it, and that is fine. In about three minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. Many churches in America run a basketball league for children. There may be six teams, and forty families.
Every week the families ask the same questions. When is our game? Who do we play? When is practice? Which door of the gym do we use?
And when there is snow, and the games are cancelled, the league leader must phone forty families, one by one. Some hear the news too late, and drive to an empty gym.
GameDay puts all of this on one page. Every family keeps the same link on their phone. The league leader writes the schedule once, and everyone reads it.
Who uses it? Parents and players, to read. The league leader, often called the league director, writes it. In Kenya you could think of a school or church football league with many teams.
One important thing. In this app, families only read. There is nothing to type and nothing to save. The league director changes the page for everyone.
The teams you will see are an example league, with made-up teams, to show how it works. A box with a dashed border at the top says so.
Now let us walk through the page slowly, from the top.

lines.t: At the top is the name, GameDay, and the name of the league.

lines: Just under the top, there is a place for a red banner. Most days it is empty, so you do not see it. When games are cancelled, for example because of snow, the league director puts a red banner here. It is the first thing every family sees. That one banner replaces forty phone calls.
Next comes Upcoming games. The games are grouped by day. Each day has a white card with the date at the top.
On each line you see two teams with the letters vs between them, the gym name, and on the right, the time of the game. Vs is short for versus, which means against.
Games that have already been played go away by themselves. So the first card is always the next game day.

lines.t: Next is Standings. This table shows how well each team is doing. W means wins. L means losses. The team at the top has a crown.

lines: If two teams have the same wins and losses, the table shows the letter T before the number. T means tied, or equal.
Then comes Practice times. Practice means training. Each team has one evening in the week, with the start and end time.
At the bottom is The gym. It gives the name and address of the gym, which door to use, when the food stand is open, and what to bring.
At the very bottom there is a link called Start fresh. In GameDay it has nothing to erase, because you never save anything here.
The times use AM and PM. AM is morning, and PM is afternoon or evening. So 9:00 AM is nine in the morning.

In the test, you will be a parent with a child in one team. You will need to find answers quickly, the way a busy parent does on a Friday night. If anything is hard to find, say so. That is exactly what we want to learn.

challenge.intro: Now you are Mike, and Emma plays for Gold Rush. Nobody will tell you where to look. Find each answer on the page and write it in your own words. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open GameDay. If the welcome card shows, tap 'skip the tour' → 'Let’s go ›'. There is nothing to erase: GameDay never saves anything you type. (Verified 10 Oct: the bottom link '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' only says 'There is nothing saved in this app yet — nothing to erase.')
challenge.challengeNote: GameDay saves nothing on the phone. Families only read the page; the league director writes the schedule into the app itself. So the app cannot be 'started empty' and no answer can be read from localStorage. Every task is a find-it question the student answers in writing (check = null, selfReport). The dates follow today (the example league always shows next Saturday), so the answers stay the same all week.

tasks.text: When is Gold Rush's next game, at what time, and against which team?
tasks.selfReport: Write the day, the time and the other team.
tasks.answer: This coming Saturday at 9:00 AM, against Blue Thunder (first card under Upcoming games).
tasks.hint: Look under Upcoming games. The first card is the next game day. Find the line with Gold Rush.

tasks.text: Emma has practice (training) every week. Which day and what time?
tasks.selfReport: Write the day and the time.
tasks.hint: Scroll down past the table to Practice times.

tasks.text: Which team is first in the league right now, and how many games has it won and lost?
tasks.selfReport: Write the team and its wins and losses.
tasks.answer: Blue Thunder, 2 wins and 0 losses (the crown in Standings).
tasks.hint: Look at the Standings table. W means wins, L means losses.

tasks.text: You arrive at the gym. Which door do you use, and what must Emma bring with her?
tasks.selfReport: Write the door and what to bring.
tasks.answer: Door 4, by the playground; bring her own water bottle (The gym, at the bottom).
tasks.hint: The very last card on the page, The gym, tells you.

tasks.text: On Saturday morning there is heavy snow. How will you know quickly if the games are cancelled?
tasks.selfReport: Write where you would look and what you would see.
tasks.answer: A red banner appears at the very top of the page (the league director puts it there). No phone calls needed.
tasks.hint: Think about the video: what appears at the top of the page when games are cancelled?

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: one page for a church sports league: games, standings, practice times, the gym
families only read it; the league leader updates it for everyone
a red banner at the top tells everyone at once when games are cancelled

daily.task: Open GameDay and look up one team’s next game. Write it in the box below: which team, when, and against whom.
daily.ask: Which team, when, and against whom?

explore.name: 🚨 The top · red banner
explore.try: Read the league name and any red banner.

explore.name: 📅 Upcoming games
explore.try: Find the next Saturday. Read each game: teams, gym, time.

explore.name: 🏆 Standings
explore.try: Check the team on top has the most wins.

explore.name: ⏰ Practice times
explore.try: Find one team’s practice day and time.

explore.name: 📍 The gym
explore.try: Read the address and details. Turn the phone sideways and back.

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open every line in it: Aa (size), 🎤 Tell it, 👪 My Circle, ✨ Ask an AI, 🎬 Take the tour again. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
